payload.summary: Home Assistant CrashLoopBackOff (exitCode 100, 4+ restarts), API unreachable at 172.16.2.237:8123. Time-correlates with the FP2 notify-only detector build; automation.fp2_keuken_offline_detectie + 'FP2 Keuken - Weer online' throwing UndefinedError on trigger.to_state/from_state. Build agent halted mid-regeneration. Household automation DOWN.

payload.leading_hypothesis: exitCode 100 is HA signalling restart-requested, not a crash. Repeated homeassistant.restart calls during the automation build produced rapid successive exits, which Kubernetes interpreted as CrashLoopBackOff and penalised with backoff delay. Outage was real (~10 min API-unreachable) but the cause looks procedural, not a broken config.
payload.mitigation: halted the FP2 detector build agent mid-regeneration; disabled automation.fp2_keuken_offline_detectie and automation.fp2_keuken_weer_online (half-built, broken templates, unvalidated)
payload.not_yet_proven: no direct evidence linking the FP2 template errors to the exits; those errors only fire when the automation triggers, and FP2 has been healthy
payload.state: HA recovered on its own after the 5th restart; 2/2 Running, API HTTP 200
payload.user_impact: HA API + all automations unavailable roughly 09:21-09:33 CEST

payload.cause: ha-engineer called homeassistant.restart 4 times in ~7 minutes (09:15:30, 09:16:30, 09:18:30, 09:22:30) to apply automation edits during the FP2 detector build
payload.corrective_action: standing rule - never homeassistant.restart to apply automation changes, use automation.reload. Rebuild used ZERO restarts (restartCount held at 5).
payload.damage_mechanism: kubelet exponential backoff (10/20/40/80s). The final exit at 09:29:30 cost an 80s gap instead of ~10s purely because of the four preceding restarts.
payload.found_during_remediation: notify.mobile_app_s25_ultra_sander does not exist; 3 call sites incl. alertmanager_critical_notify -> critical cluster alert pushes have been silently failing. Separate change dispatched.
payload.impact_correction: NOT a continuous 12-min outage as atlas first reported. kube_pod_container_status_ready shows three discrete ~60s unready windows: 09:17:30-09:18:30, 09:21:30-09:22:30, 09:30:30-09:31:30. HA served normally 09:22:30-09:30:00.
payload.template_errors: real but NOT causal - log noise, they do not exit the process
payload.unattributed: the 5th exit at 09:29:07 is NOT explained. atlas made no HA write before 09:31:30; ha-engineer restart at that moment was rejected by the permission system; no automation/script/config calls homeassistant.restart. Left open rather than guessed.

payload.atlas_disclaimer: Atlas confirms he made no write to HA before automation.turn_off on the two FP2 automations, which was after 09:31:30 when the API was already back. Not his.
payload.hestia_disclaimer: Not mine. My homeassistant.restart at that moment was rejected by the permission system and per tool semantics did not execute.
payload.log_evidence: Recovered from kubectl logs --previous on the pre-restart container. At 09:29:07.126 a full YAML configuration re-read begins (annotatedyaml parsing /config/themes/..., bluetooth wrapper re-registration) — the config-validation pass that homeassistant.restart performs — and the next line is 'Found 2 non-daemonic threads.', a graceful stop. Signature of a REQUESTED restart, not a crash: no traceback, no fatal error, no OOM, container exit 100 = HA restart-requested.
payload.recommendation: To make future restarts attributable, either remove 'call_service' from the recorder exclude list (cost: recorder growth) or add a logger override for homeassistant.core. Separate change; not executed.
ruled_out: not a Kubernetes eviction or OOM kill
not the FP2 UndefinedError (09:22:42, 6.5 min earlier, non-fatal condition-evaluation error)
payload.spinoff_defect: This incident's remediation surfaced a 12-day silent failure of the critical-alert push path. Tracked and fixed under chg-2026-07-23-006 (3 dead notify call sites; 1 critical alert / 4 pushes lost).
payload.status: UNATTRIBUTED — closing this line of enquiry unless new evidence appears
payload.topic: 5th HA exit at 2026-07-23 09:29:07 CEST — formally recorded as UNATTRIBUTED
payload.unproven_hypothesis_only: A human-initiated restart from the HA UI, companion app or a kiosk session remains possible but is NOT evidenced. Noted only because 09:25:11 shows kiosk service activity (switch.pixel_tablet_scherm), proving a browser/app session was live in that window. Stated as a hypothesis, not a conclusion.
payload.why_unattributable: HA does not log the calling context/user of homeassistant.restart at INFO level, and configuration.yaml recorder excludes event_types: [call_service], so no audit row exists. The automation domain is also excluded from the recorder.

payload.summary: chg-2026-07-30-003 aborted at device 1 of 9: the landing check required the reserved IP as well as the target VLAN, so a device that HAD correctly moved to IOT-VLAN (but got pool IP 172.16.5.109 instead of reserved 172.16.4.21) was scored as failed and rolled back, aborting the run. 0/9 migrated. No household impact: no speaker lost power, the relay was never toggled, rollback verified (device back at 172.16.3.109, HA reports on/5.4W). Fix: accept any IOT-VLAN address as landed and treat a wrong IP as correctable, not fatal; also lengthen the settle time after the reservation write (pilot had 21s and worked, run had 2s and did not).

payload.note: Fix validated by chg-2026-07-31-001 single-device rehearsal on the production script. Failure mode did not reproduce; device landed on its reserved 172.16.4.25. Load-bearing fix was the corrected success criterion + re-DHCP nudge, not the settle time.
Two consecutive clean rehearsals on the production script, exercising both code paths (nudge-needed on Terras, direct-land on Achtertuin). Failure mode has not reproduced.

payload.summary: Non-curl clients on the Mac Mini get EHOSTUNREACH to Cilium L2-announced LoadBalancer VIPs (172.16.2.237 HA, 172.16.2.240 k8s API) while curl reaches the same host:port reliably. Deterministic: 5/5 curl success vs 5/5 python socket failure, interleaved, same IP. NOT the cluster (API answers 401 to curl), NOT the Claude Code sandbox (fails with it disabled), NOT routing (route get identical to working hosts), NOT ARP (entry present, points at master01), NOT source-address selection (explicit bind does not help). Real devices (172.16.2.1, 172.16.2.81) connect fine from python. Suspicion: Apple Network.framework vs raw BSD sockets interacting with Cilium L2 announcement / MAC-per-VIP behaviour. IMPACT: kubectl unusable from this Mac; any non-curl LAN tooling against cluster VIPs is broken. Workaround in use: drive Home Assistant via its REST API with curl, which works.

payload.cluster_health: Never impaired. All 6 nodes Ready throughout.
payload.fix: Grant Local Network permission in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Local Network. Responsible process chain here is /opt/homebrew/bin/tmux -> zsh -> claude -> zsh, so tmux and/or the terminal app and/or Claude need the toggle. A detached tmux SERVER becomes its own responsible process, so tmux is the likely entry and the tmux server must be restarted after granting.
payload.interim_workaround: System curl IS permitted, so the k8s API can be reached directly with the kubeconfig client cert: extract certificate-authority-data / client-certificate-data / client-key-data and curl https://172.16.2.240:6443/... Verified working: returned all 6 nodes Ready. Extracted key material was shredded from /tmp afterwards.
payload.proof: Identical Python code, two binaries, same destinations: /usr/bin/python3 -> 172.16.2.240:6443 CONNECTED and 1.1.1.1:443 CONNECTED. /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 -> 172.16.2.240:6443 errno=65, 1.1.1.1:443 CONNECTED. System binaries (curl, nc, perl) all worked; Homebrew/mise binaries (python3, openssl, kubectl) all failed, and ONLY to the local subnet.
payload.root_cause: macOS Local Network Privacy on macOS 26.5.2. Non-Apple binaries must be granted Local Network permission to reach the DIRECTLY-ATTACHED subnet. Without it, connect() to on-link hosts returns EHOSTUNREACH (errno 65) while routed/internet traffic is unaffected — which is exactly the pattern that made this look like a Cilium/VIP problem.
payload.why_it_misled_us: It was never about Cilium L2-announced VIPs. 172.16.2.240 and .237 are simply on the local subnet, as are the nodes and the NAS. Traffic to 172.16.4.20 (IOT-VLAN, ROUTED via the gateway) always worked from the same blocked binaries, which is what made the VIP theory look plausible. Also ruled out along the way: the Claude Code sandbox (fails with it disabled), routing (single interface, clean table), ARP (resolves on demand), source-address binding, proxies, VPN/utun0 (IPv6 link-local only), bridge0 (inactive).

payload.summary: health-notify CronJob (observability) failing daily since at least 22 Aug: calls notify.mobile_app_s25_ultra_sander which does not exist in HA (actual service is notify.mobile_app_galaxy_s25_ultra). 10 Error pods retained, 2 per day. The stale name is baked into the container image ghcr.io/vdhict/cluster-health:sha-de00b79 (/scripts/notify.py), NOT in repo YAML, which is why the July remediation of inc-2026-07-23-001 fixed HA's automations but missed this call site. IMPACT LIMITED: HA-side alerting is healthy - automations.yaml uses the correct service at all 6 call sites incl. the Alertmanager critical path, so critical cluster alerts were NOT affected during the holiday. Only the daily cluster-health digest push was lost. Fix requires an image rebuild or an env-var override of the notify target.

Trapkast UPS (stroomblok ch1) is energised but powers nothing (user confirmed 2026-08-30). ch1 draws a flat ~10.2W, lifetime 673.9 kWh - the largest single channel on that strip - for a UPS protecting no load. ~90 kWh/yr wasted if left. SEPARATE UNRESOLVED DISCREPANCY: the Innr plug named UPS (0xa4c138bdc1d57e65, area Trapkast) does NOT track ch1. Ten simultaneous samples showed ch1 pinned at 10.2W while the Innr swung 17-56W, so they are measuring DIFFERENT loads. Either the Innr is not on ch1, or it sits on the UPS output rather than its input. Not resolved by toggling because the Innr feeds an unidentified load. Needs a look at the cupboard.

payload.note: Partially addressed. The pump Innr was freed and moved to the server UPS input, revealing ~330W of previously unmetered load. The Trapkast UPS on ch1 still powers nothing at ~10W. The separate discrepancy - the Innr named UPS not tracking ch1 - remains open and needs a look at the cupboard.

payload.caveat: Cutting mains makes the UPS alarm and run down its battery. Repeated deep discharge shortens battery life. If the intent is to retire or store it, power it down properly first and then remove mains; if the intent is to reuse it, better to repurpose it than leave it cycling.
payload.powerwalker_shutdown: PowerWalker UPSes need the On/Off button held, not tapped - 1s on VFI 1000T/E LCD, 2s on VI 600-1500 CSW, model dependent. BUT the likely reason it would not switch off: on models with bypass enabled, the output sockets STAY LIVE from mains even after the UPS is switched off, so it looks like it never powered down. PowerWalker own manual says the mains must be disconnected in that case.
payload.practical_route_here: The Trapkast UPS sits on stroomblok ch1, which is individually switchable. switch.stroomblok (renamed Stroomblok Trapkast ch1 - UPS) cuts its mains from HA - exactly what the manual asks for - without touching the button.

payload.CORRECTION: My earlier PowerWalker guidance was WRONG for this model. I passed on a search snippet about the VFI/CSW series (hold the button 1-2s; bypass keeps outputs live). The user then told me the exact model - VI 2200 SHL IEC - and the official VI SH/SHL 650-2200VA manual, which explicitly lists PowerWalker VI 2200 SHL, says something different.
payload.actual_manual_text: Section VI Turn On/Off the Unit: Turn on the UPS unit by pressing the power switch. Turn off the UPS unit by pressing again the power switch. A SIMPLE PRESS - no 2-second hold.
payload.audible_alarm_reference: every 10s = battery mode, every 1s = battery low, every 0.5s = overload, continuous = fault.
payload.how_to_confirm: Look at the LCD. If output voltage reads 000 it is in off charging mode i.e. already off.
payload.how_to_reach_zero_watts: Only by removing mains. ch1 is individually switchable: switch.stroomblok (Stroomblok Trapkast ch1 - UPS) does it from HA. Caveat: a lead-acid UPS left unpowered self-discharges, so for long-term storage it needs periodic recharging.
payload.likely_what_actually_happened: The manual documents an OFF CHARGING MODE with its own LCD screen, and notes the output voltage always displays 000 in off charging mode. That is the UPS switched OFF but still on mains charging its battery. It still draws power. So the user probably DID switch it off successfully - the ~10.2W on ch1 is the battery charger plus the units own electronics, not a failure to power down. Consistent with ch1 reading a flat 10.2W.
payload.no_bypass_on_this_model: The VI SH/SHL manual contains ZERO occurrences of bypass and ZERO of standby. This line-interactive series has no bypass mode, so the earlier bypass-keeps-outputs-live explanation cannot apply here.
payload.source: PowerWalker VI SH/SHL (650-2200VA) manual EN, extracted with pdftotext from the official plytix-hosted PDF; model list confirms VI 2200 SHL is in scope.
